Assistant: I need to expose the new scoped activation helper inside `nmp-core` only; it is not a new public product API.

Assistant: Now I’m wiring the kernel’s observed-interest open to activate with the declared interest shape instead of activating as an all-event tap.

Assistant: The replay path also has to use relay-aware matching, otherwise a relay-pinned group view can replay cached events from another host with the same `#h` value. I’m patching replay selection next.

Assistant: The kernel now activates observed projections with the opened interest shape. I’m moving the NIP-29 group-feed composer onto the new `ObservedProjectionRegistrar` so it gets the same close semantics and carries relay pins in replay shapes.

Assistant: I caught a tooling mistake: `apply_patch` defaulted to the root checkout for the first code edits. I’m reversing only those mistaken code edits there, keeping the required `WIP.md` entry, and then applying the patch to the isolated worktree with absolute paths.

Assistant: Yes. I initially narrowed the follow-up too much around `#2113`; the live queue shows the related P0 stack is `#2088`, `#2090`, and `#2091` under the closed `#2089` umbrella, with `#2113` as a separate P2 sibling. I’m correcting that now and will keep the PR scoped to the declared observed-projection seam rather than pretending the dynamic-source work covers those observer issues.

Assistant: The accidental root edits are not present now: root only shows the unrelated `android/` and `ios/` directories. I’m checking the live WIP entry and then I’ll apply the actual changes in the agent worktree only.

Assistant: The WIP entry is present and the implementation worktree is clean on `origin/master`. I’m going to patch the worktree now: first the core live-delivery scope bug, then the NIP-29 group-feed caller, then the docs that currently teach the old observer behavior.

Assistant: The key bug is clear in code: `open_interest_with_observer_replay` still calls `activate_observer`, which promotes the projection into unfiltered global delivery. That means a view opened through the new declared projection seam hydrates correctly, then still receives every future event.

Assistant: I’m also keeping search in mind: it already has its own FTS cache lane and suppresses replay, so this change should not try to make `search` locally evaluable. The scoped delivery can still use the wire dimensions plus relay pin and leave query-text filtering to the NIP-50 projection/store path.

Assistant: I’m editing the worktree now. The core change is a new shape predicate for observed projections, including relay-pin provenance, and a scoped activation path that keeps muted replay semantics without rejoining unfiltered fan-out.

Assistant: The relay-pin check uses store provenance for relay-delivered events and preserves local read-your-writes for non-search pinned feeds. NIP-50 search is deliberately excluded from that local-publish exception because search text is relay/store evaluated, not locally inferred.

Assistant: I need one visibility cleanup in the observer slot: the delivery enum has to match the field visibility because the registration struct exposes that field to its parent module for tests/bookkeeping.

Assistant: Next I’m wiring the scoped activation through the command exports and kernel replay path so observed projections use it, while legacy live taps keep the old unfiltered `activate_observer`.

Assistant: The public compatibility is intentional here: bare `activate_observer` remains for live taps, and observed projections get the new scoped path. I’m not removing the old function because it is a distinct live-tap behavior, not a second way to open a hydrating projection.

Assistant: Now I’m changing replay activation itself. The shape used for live delivery is the actual registered interest shape, so account-scoped opens and relay-pinned opens keep their normal routing identity but no longer leak future unrelated events into the projection.
 [...] Assistant: The docs audit matches the issue audit: several guides still describe old all-event observers as the recommended read-model path. I’m updating the durable docs in place rather than adding a new planning file, per repo doctrine.

Assistant: I’m making the docs distinguish two read-model cases explicitly: `register_live_event_tap` is a live-only all-event tap, while `open_observed_projection` is the hydrating, interest-scoped projection door. That removes the stale advice that every read model should be a global observer.
 [...] - #2090 and #2091 remain open intentionally.
